steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 2 ½-quart baking dish with cooking spray.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add eggplant, onion, and garlic; cook and stir until vegetables begin to soften, about 8 minutes. Stir in zucchini, tomatoes, bell pepper, basil, parsley, salt, and black pepper; bring to a boil, stirring frequently. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil; stir in ravioli and return to a boil. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 3 to 5 minutes. Drain.
Transfer ravioli to bottom of the prepared baking dish; spoon hot vegetable mixture over top. Sprinkle with mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbling and cheese melted, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ratatouille Bake
raw_recipe.description: This ratatouille bake recipe includes garden veggies like eggplant and zucchini, layered onto ready-made cheese ravioli, and topped with mozzarella cheese.

review.reviewBody: Very clever and delicious idea! I opened a can of pureed tomatoes instead of diced, so mine was more saucy than it should have been, but it worked. I used a smaller but deep casserole so I put a little sauce in the bottom, layer of ravioli, veggies and sauce, more ravioli and topped with the rest of the veggies and sauce, and cheese. While I love traditional ratatouille, I usually need to have something else with it as it's not too filling for me - the ravioli makes this a complete, and delicious, meal! Thanks for sharing!

I made this delicious recipe. The only thing I did differently is that I did not use raviolis and I did not make it as a casserole. Instead I sauteed all the veggies and simmered in a dutch oven on top of the stove for at least an hour. The more it simmered the more the flavor. It was dynamite!! Yummy!! Then, I cooked some penne pasta and put the tomato soaked veggies with the pasta and topped it with Romano cheese and wow!! What a wonderful dish!! You can add cooked Italian sausage or chicken to the dish and make it a meat lovers and veggie dish. Wonderful recipe! I'll be making this again soon!! Thank you. :-)

I used all veggies from my garden and fresh parsley & basil. And didn’t bother to boil the ravioli. I just placed them on the dish while I cooked the veggies. It was absolutely delicious! So good I’m writing my first review after over 15 years of using this site for recipes and inspiration: it’s THAT delicious!

Great recipe and I also made lots of changes:
- used left over Homemade Pasta instead of the raviolli
- used homemade Marina Sauce (with a bit of Beyond Meat) instead of canned tomatoes (it had lots of fresh basil in it)
- added 1/2 cup of Stout for robust flavor
- used 2x the eggplant (basically a whole eggplant, peeled and chopped and soaked in salted water for 2hrs).

This was very tasty but I did make some alterations. I made the ratatouille per this recipe and added a couple tablespoons of tomato paste. The dish is great as is. However, here are my alterations: Instead of the ravioli, I used pre-cooked polenta. I baked the sliced polenta in my toaster oven for 15 minutes, then sprinkled some cheese on it before topping it with the ratatouille and more cheese. I also didn't bake the dish. I cooked the veggies in a large pot and covered it to simmer on low for at least 30 minutes before adding it to the polenta. This is also good with cooked hot Italian sausage if you want to make this for your carnivore loved ones :)

My husband said this was a hit. This is my experience: I used a 7×11×2 inch casserole which is 2 1/2 qt. I bought a 25 oz bag of frozen ravioli (size of ravioli 2" × 1 1/2"). I weighed 8 oz out on my kitchen scale. That came out to 18 ravioli. When cooked and placed in the bottom of the casserole it covered the dish completely. For reference, if this is 6 servings that's 3 ravioli per serving. That makes me think this is a side dish. But, adjust accordingly and you get 3 servings having 6 ravioli plus luscious veggies making for a meal. Serve with Texas toast. I used a full cup of shredded part skim mozzarella, can of diced tomatoes, 3 tablespoons each of fresh basil and parsley (had them from my herb garden). Calorie wise it comes out about the same. My husband added shredded parmesan to his and was satisfied with 4 ravioli. This will become a regular item at our house. I imagine the leftovers tomorrow will be even better. One other thing comes to mind. The 1/2 teaspoon of salt wasn't enough. Next time I'll use a full teaspoon. Either way it's easy enough to add salt at the table if you need it.

I made it with roasted eggplant & zucchini. I used about 2 tsp. minced garlic which was plenty! I added about 1 1/2 cups spaghetti sauce & 1/2 c. water then served over spaghetti noodles. This made about 12 servings @ 12 ounces.

It was delicious! I doubled the tortellini and baked in a 9x13 glass dish. I also poured 1/2 jar of spaghetti sauce over tortellini before adding cooked vegetables to add more flavor. My husband and I liked it and had enough left over for another meal. I imagine it will be even tastier tomorrow !

I'm reviewing this recipe after the 2nd time I made it. Fabulous! That's all! I did add smoked bacon this time....I cut 1/3rd package of bacon into small prices...sauté it...removed the nicely browned bacon into a separate bowl and proceeded with the recipe as written. I used a smoked mozzarella ravioli and late summer vegetables purchased from my local farmers' market. I also subbed fresh heirloom cherry tomatoes for the canned version. Yum. I also used a mix of fresh mozzarella, provolone and Parmesan cheeses. This is probably the recipe I look most forward to at the end of fresh tomato/Farmers' Market season.

I diced an Anaheim pepper (instead of bell pepper), added a few more fresh garlic to the vegetables. I added 1/2 cup parmigiana and mozzarella into the vegetables before topping the ravioli. 

It was a very good meal, a nice change of pace. Thank you for posting.

Delicious vegetarian option! The prep work was a lot, but I think worth it. I used fresh tomatoes in lieu of canned, and about 15oz ravioli rather than 8oz. I would say this feeds 4 adults rather than 6. Will definitely make again.
good
I did not have zucchini but had everything else. I think I'd add some sauce or use marinara sauce instead of diced tomatoes.
I love Ratatouille! I've made many variations on the classic recipe over the years. This I a nice recipe for a bit of a change. Freezes well to.
This is a wonderful recipe and 1 of my husband's favorites!!
It wasn't bad but won't make again.

Cooked all veggie's in my large cast iron skillet all at once. I added hot peppers, butternut squash, chicken sausage cut into 1/2's then 4's. A dash of my dry merlot and added fresh grated parmesan cheese on top mixed with mozzarella. Really good.

This dish is excellent very flavorful and delicious. I wanted to make a meal out of it so the only changes I made was to use beef ravioli and I cooked the vegetables with about 1/2 cup of beef broth. I will definitely make this recipe again!
Followed the recipe but used twice as much mozzarella and ravioli-- Perfect!

This recipe is easy, but still very delicious and even a little fancy. I recommend you to try this. I didn’t need to make any changes, except I just cooked normal noodles instead of ravioli. A big success!
